Use case: precise-object-edit. The attached image is the user-selected FULL COIN DESIGN, a beautiful silver engraved ex-libris certification medal in a triptych: blank front, narrow edge, elaborate reverse with open-book seal and a certification register. Preserve this exact design direction, overall layout, sculpted folio icon with three incised lines on each page, rays inside seal, purposeful engraved foliage, cartouche geometry, rim and alternating diagonal/plain edge craft, antique-satin silver material and polish hierarchy, charcoal studio background. Keep front ENTIRELY EMPTY, same as reference. No new central front motif or text. This is a visual typography/real-content design study, not an actual issued certificate.

Replace ALL placeholder text on the reverse with the following VERIFIED first chapter content, and recompose ONLY the certification-register typography so it looks professionally designed with the longer content. No XXX or invented information. Keep upper series arc exactly "THE SECOND LANGUAGE".
The register header: "CHAPTER 01", medium small Roman serif capitals.
The central primary title is exact Chinese text "地图上的那条线" (seven characters: 地 图 上 的 那 条 线). Engraved elegant Song/Ming serif letterforms, confident and beautifully spaced, NOT handwritten or a pasted flat font. Give it one clean centred line within the cartouche.
Immediately underneath, a smaller English secondary title EXACTLY "The Line on the Map", a refined humanist serif, perfectly centred and subordinate.
Below the lower engraved separator, a compact static status label exactly "CERTIFIED".
Then one very small, clearly distinct lower line EXACTLY "CHAPTER DATE · 02 OCT 2026". This date is the real CHAPTER DATE, NOT the certification date. Keep the explicit words CHAPTER DATE visible. No invented pass date, score, certificate number or signature.
Keep the register coherent and uncrowded: reduce or reposition its decorative horizontal separators slightly if needed to make proper title and date breathing room, do not shrink the title to microscopic size. Preserve the original small book seal and overall ex-libris aesthetic. The information hierarchy is chapter number -> Chinese chapter title -> smaller English title -> certification label and clearly labelled chapter date.

Finish should have tangible purposeful silver: densely fine satin ground, controlled dark intaglio recesses, delicate hand-burnished bevels/bright engraved strokes, not foil wrinkles, chunky global noise or uniform grey plastic. Text should read as true precision metal engraving/relief with consistent light and depth. Keep one complete-object three-view design submission, front left, edge middle, reverse right, large clear reverse, similar scale to reference. No external captions, no extra logos, no additional theme illustration, no fog/particles, no actual coins stacked or props. High-quality collectible product concept photography with warm-neutral silver, not gold.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Preserve this exact user-selected ex-libris silver medal, the full triptych with completely blank front, decorative side and elegant bookplate reverse. Make ONE typographic variation using the same REAL first chapter information: give the English title the primary hierarchy, Chinese the smaller secondary hierarchy. Do not change the small sculpted book seal, original icon-derived page motif, surrounding engraving, border, body, silver material, lighting or cameras.
Reverse upper series remains exactly "THE SECOND LANGUAGE". Register header remains exactly "CHAPTER 01". Primary title, in a beautiful engraved serif, must be two deliberately spaced centred lines EXACTLY:
"THE LINE"
"ON THE MAP"
Immediately beneath it, a smaller elegant Chinese Song/Ming engraved title EXACTLY "地图上的那条线".
Then the lower separator and a small static label "CERTIFIED".
The distinct very small footer remains EXACTLY "CHAPTER DATE · 02 OCT 2026". This is the actual chapter date; do not replace it with a certification date.
Rebalance the small inner separators and title whitespace tastefully to accommodate two English lines without a cramped bottom or tiny primary words. No actual certificate number or score, no XXX, no added illustration, no gold, no particles or smoke. Preserve the entirely blank front and clear tactile thin side. Render the text as sharply engraved/intaglio metal with consistent microbevels, not a flat Photoshop print. Main title should have quiet medallic dignity and be visually subordinate to the overall complete object, not a giant signboard.
